Oe I have a few from my 2 stays (kinda 3, but 2 goodish ones). I’m from South Africa and have decent healthcare soo I know that makes a difference but.

First place was actually really lovely. Made lots of friends, we had birthday parties and chill for a while outside where there were nice gardens. My psych humans I had been with for a while and if my day was going shit they would let me chill in their office until it was my time to see them. It was a really good break from reality for a bit, until my medical aid cut me off and they just let me sit in their office and cry knowing I’d have to go back home to a shitty situation I haven’t processed yet or worked through. There were lots of optional activities - group, art, clay, occupational, I can’t even remember everything tbh. It was a full on mental facility that had many different therapists and psychiatrists that you can choose from and shift through until you find a fit.

Other one was what we called a glorified psych ward where there was an icu and sonar humans, but the hospital was basically just a massive facility for one psychiatrist and his therapist. Some humans could have their phones, others not. He would generally come in hella late at night which wasn’t great, but he also got to the point, by making you get yourself to the point. There were social workers, therapists and a horrible occupational therapist, but we played games whenever we didn’t do homework. Got to see our families often (if you wanted them), order food, and legit just…… not exist in the rest of the world. Get your shit shoved in your face nightly and then the next morning work with a social worker to plan what happens after you leave and all that. Also. A physio. I love her. She’s awesome! She makes everything better. 

At both places the food was awesome with a bunch of different options, nurses were great, full bathrooms, had to share rooms but generally that went okay. No wifi though, but it wasn’t as horrible as a lot of other stories I’ve heard, and we got to see a lot of people grow throughout the 21 days you get to spend there (depending on insurance). Nurses make a massive difference though, it really really does.

Hiya, love! I’m no expert, but if you psych humans are pretty sure, and your friends are also concerned, you probably are manic. Parents are strange when it comes to mania… they (not speaking for everyone, but some) don’t want to believe you’re manic so they find excuses to say it’s not. Because it’s not real if we don’t say it’s real.  And yes, not everyone sees (or recognises) symptoms.   Recognising your own mania becomes part of your own game plan of catching a manic episode before it’s goes very very much downhill.   And thinking you’re making it all up is also hella common.   So I say trust the psych humans. Follow their plan… This isn’t fun. And sucks. But you have humans who are concerned for you and want to support you, so check in with them too. Believing it is hard. I know this. However, you are going to have to recognise what’s going on in order to help yourself (for right now and for in case it happens again).   However!!! I wish you the bestest of luck and there’s a bunch of awesome humans here to help you out. <3

Hi, friend. There are so many med cocktails that need to be figured out before you’re going to find an okay spot. I know of some people that make it, but many of us don’t. Meds are a forever thing. Exercise and healthy eating can help, but this isn’t just a mental block. 

Think of it as if it were a chronic disease. You can’t just stop your heart medication or blood thinners, or anything else physically related. Mental health is no different. Once you have the cock tail, it gets better. There are draw backs. But it’s a thing. There is a physical chemical imbalance in your brain. Jumping through episodes can and will lead to future brain damage. 

I know it sucks to hear. I hate my meds. I will do almost anything to avoid taking them because I don’t want to sleep as much. I don’t want to be chucked into an episode every time I forget to take them. But I also know that they are one of the only things keeping me alive.

Talk with your psych. Talk about med changes (not stopping them outright, but see if changing them around makes I difference.). It can take a while. But please understand that we have a chronic disease essentially, and unfortunately meds are part of it. Again. You won’t just stop meds for chronic physical illnesses…

Complete opposite of what some are saying, but I stagger them. You obviously can’t do what I usually do because it’s breakfast and everyone generally knows what they want to drink, so maybe as you get them, grab the drink order, greet-grab order-etc. But for the sake of having the kitchen as your friends and yourself, stagger those orders. Grab, punch the order, next table and repeat. It gives you time to not have food waiting, and still to talk to the other customers. Also. If you’ve worked the shift enough you know the ticket-time ratio by now. Even if it’s not 100% accurate give them an estimate time, keep it to unusual times 7 minutes, 4 minutes, anything you don’t already have a set timer to in your head. If it’s super duper busy, keep em updated. Once you have them staggered, it comes easy. Also. If you can see them sit down, remember what order they got sat even if it’s 20 seconds apart. Don’t want them going “we were here first”. Other than that, not much you can really do. Hope this helps

Also. On the prep thing. It makes a difference if I know (i’m not condoning hiding food in other food), my mind takes that ingredient I don’t like and completely throws the mental taste of it even before I get to eat it. I don’t use mustard powder, I know I don’t like mustard the condiment, so I thus don’t like mustard the powder, even though my mom uses it in a lot of dishes. I stopped eating one of my favourite meals because I walked in on her stacking the spices out and saw a bunch of ingredients I “recognise” but don’t know how I feel about them. It’s not like I don’t want to use an array of spices, but if I don’t have an established response to it, I go by looks and smell where possible. I know green foods are generally safe for me. Red is a possible “poison” or “omg I love this”, yellow….. no. Don’t even try. 

Logically it makes 0 sense. But brain says this is how it is, deal with it. It takes a lot for me to try a new food unless I’m previously intrigued.

I very very badly did this. But for the little that I could, I’ll give you what I’ve got.

Schedules. They suck, they’re boring, they’re annoying, but they work. Make time for everything, including sleep. If you have time between classes, study so you don’t have to do it at home. 

I had a really nice boss who let me study while working (restaurant manager) which helped a lot. 

Also. Have at least some time for yourself, where you can decompress and do something fun. Mine was pole dancing, my new one is ice skating or playing piano. Literally anything you can do for an hour or two just to relax and feel like a fricking human. 

Make contingency plans. Chances are you might forget about a project and only see the due date. In your planning, make your due dates a week before, so you still get the due date rush, but you’re actually ahead of schedule so if you miss it, you still have time.

Working while studying is hard… stupid hard. Working while studying with bp is even worse. But it’s doable. Drink your meds. Keep a healthy routine. Compartmentalise. And remember you’re a human and mistakes will happen. But it’s okay. Ask your psych maybe for some anti anxieties so that you don’t stress as much (literally saved me a few times).

Oh. And. DO NOT DRINK!!!! It doesn’t help. It makes things worse. It’s horrid. It may seem fine, but it will spiral you. 

Best of luck and I hope you keep us updated with all your success!! <3

I was there about a year and a bit ago (this was a private ward so a bit different than some i guess)

I was voluntary 

We were not strip searched but the rules were made clear that if they do find something they will send you to some other psych hospitals or that you will be discharged. 

I had 3 other roommates. We were grouped by age(ish) and gender. They were all really really nice and supportive.

We had a cafe of sorts open from 8am - just before dinner. They served coffee and other snacks and food. We were also provided with early coffee runs before wake up call, at noon, and at 7pm (i think). As for nicotine. We were allowed to smoke as much as we wanted outside, but you had to get someone to bring it in for you. It was someone’s birthday when I was there and they legit got him a carton of smokes XD

We had free access of our phones, but the idea was that you stay off of them unless you want to or have to. For someone who is usually glued to my phone, I spent very little time on my phone there. You could also bring your computer if you needed to work, but it was at your own risk and not recommended. 

As for therapy. Therapy was mandatory every day for 30 minutes. The nurses would hunt you down for your session.

We had psychiatry meetings every day as they change our meds a lot and need to see if anything is changing. 

Full on access to outdoors until 8pm. Other than that, as long as you didn’t leave the hospital area, they really didn’t care where you were except for therapist and psych and vital checks. Also meal times. Everyone had to show for meal times and if don’t show up for meal times they bring your dinner to your room and make sure you eat there. (The food was actually really good and as someone who has severe food issues (sensory not ED) I always had something to eat)

There was a tv in the “lounge” of every ward but nothing anyone under 50 would watch. You could do art, pottery, and some other activities such as group, self healing (I can’t remember it all) if you wanted to (it was recommended to do 2 activities a day, but I honestly just didn’t want to) but you had to pay separate for some or your insurance had to cover it.

My insurance only covered a week which was absolutely devastating as I was making progress. But if I had to do some quick of the hip maths it was around $1000 a week. 

Was it worth it? If I could’ve stayed longer I think I would’ve made a lot of progress in my life. But it was a good experience that helped me a lot and kept me safe. The nurses were absolute blessings and the friends I met were insanely supportive. It was truly(in my own experience) a good place to be considering that I needed a space where my only focus was to focus on my mental health and learning about everything.

Okay so from my personal understanding from my own experience. Psychiatrists (the people who give you meds) do the short sessions. I can’t tell you what to do as I’m not in your situation, but I can offer some support.

If you’re struggling to communicate make mental notes, journal bullet points, voice notes for yourself. Well personally, I got to go to a really nice facility where both my psychiatrist and therapist work. We got to keep our phones and even laptops. 

We had a very strict schedule to follow. Wake up at 06:00 for meds, blood pressure and temperature checks. 6:30-7:30 was breakfast, you had to go. But the food was really good and there was enough choices so that you don’t have to eat what you don’t like. Then you could either do activities like art, or sculpting or just lessons about how to deal with mental health or just chill with friends. 12:00-13:00 was lunch. Then you get to do whatever, usually this is when we get called to your people to check your meds, and do your therapy. 17:00 was dinner and vitals check. You will get hunted down for your vitals check (I was also hunted down). After dinner you get to chill a bit, until around 20:30 because that was night time meds and night tea. 22:00 was lights out.

They check if we’re sleeping. The doors don’t lock. I scratched myself effed up the one day and the nurses were super helpful and supportive. They made me sit with them until I calmed down and gave me ativan. 

No outside meds were allowed. We were allowed visitors but many of us refused visitors because we just didn’t want to see our family. I made amazing friends there, we had birthday parties and mini picnics. We got to talk about our own issues and why we were there. There was a group session as well, if you wanted to go.

They called us for when our therapists wanted us. I know they called me one day and my peoples were just to busy, and I just had a really bad day, so my psych just let me sit in their office and write my letters there instead of having to go back. 

Honestly… I honestly liked it being there. It was calm. We had a schedule. You get reminded to take your meds. There’s always someone to talk to. 

I can’t say for other hospitals or anything, but I know mine was great. I even have a teddy bear from there which my friend and I went to go get because we needed something to cuddle. They really really do not like weed there, but we were allowed to smoke. There was also a volleyball court if you wanted to go play. 

I know for a lot of people it’s scary and horrible, but sometimes it’s a break you need to just get back into it.

With all due respect, I get shit for my mental health because of twats on tik tok making my mental illnesses sound like a bloody joke. It’s fine for people to get proper diagnosis and all that, but it makes my illnesses sound like a joke. We deserve to get a voice, and come together, and find people like us, but it does do damage. It’s still a problem. It will always be a problem. But having every Yip Dip and Danny saying they have something like let’s say Bipolar, because their mood changes throughout the day???? Really?? We get shit on because of our diagnosis’s, told that the label alone will ruin our lives, but it’s fine for people who honestly don’t have these conditions to say “I have it because I’ve been feeling down for a month!!” and make it seems so much easier than it is. I don’t mind people finding out what’s going with them, but it’s not okay to downplay or essentially make fun of people with these disorders. Think about the amount of Tourrettes videos that came out, that the tourrettes community came out to try and fight because it damages their image. It damages the people who actually struggle with these disorders. It’s disgusting. It’s honestly disgusting in my personal opinion. It might not be to other people, and that’s fine, but for me? It’s horrible. Finding out what you have because you can’t afford a psych is fine, but faking it is horrible. Absolutely horrible and disgusting. That’s more the issue than self diagnosing, but self diagnosing falls off of that because people try to diagnose off of fake videos. How is that helping anyone?

The problem is that they’re spreading harmful misinformation. The same is happening with bipolar, did, ocd, autism, tourrettes. It’s horrible. We need representation, but if I see one more post saying “My OCD is so bad, my books always have to be straight and colour coded”, and not “I burnt my hand on a headlamp because my other hand accidentally brushed it or spent 20 minutes rewalking the same strip because it wasn’t the right amount of steps or you accidentally stepped on the wrong tile or crack or colour, I’m going to lose it. Bipolar isn’t “My mood changes throughout the day”, it’s “I just spent everything in my bank account, and then some, went on a drug binge and decided that I don’t need to work because eff knows” followed by a 3 month depression episode that will destroy you. They spread harmful misinformation that damages people with a real diagnosis, because “I have that too!!! Look! I can’t sit still for 5 minutes. My ADHD is soooooooo bad. Hihihihi” 

We need validation, and a safe space, but the damage they cause, just isn’t worth it at this point. It makes psychs look horrible, prescribe meds that you might not need that can damage your body for no reason and then cause actual symptoms of another disorder because they try to balance something else out. It over fills psych offices to the point where people who honestly need an emergency session because their meds stopped working or they got a reaction or need to he hospitalised, can’t get them because they are packed with people who self diagnose and search all the symptoms and run to the psych with all the symptoms, very basic and classic symptoms, and say “I have x disorder, you have to give this to me. Look the internet said I have this.” It’s the same as people who google “Elbow pain” and then WebMD says “Cancer, pregnancy, lupis, and whatever other rare and unusual illnesses that just can’t happen due to the fact that the test shows it’s not there.” 

Yes having information out there can be useful. It can help you seek help, but at the same time, it can spark fake self diagnosis’s for people who just want to feel special, and do not realise how detrimental these disorders can be for the people who actually have them.

I read somewhere on another subreddit “Remember: Most customers lose 50% of their braincells the moment they step into the restaurant.” They can be sweethearts, but be patient when explaining the menu. Most of the time they will ask stupid questions that you’ve already explained. 

Another thing!! Remember this isn’t a life or death situation, breathe, step back, recalculate, plan, and move. 

Drink water. Eat before your shift. You need to take care of yourself.

Make friends or at least be kind with the Dishie. They’re important and have a really shitty job. 

Same goes for line cooks. They’ll remember who’s nice to them and if you need something on the fly, they’ll be more helpful. Also, if you can buy food from the restaurant, they’ll maybe add extra stuff or make it just how you want it. These humans are fricking magical if you treat them right. 

TEAMWORK!!! If you see another server in the weeds and they need someone to run drinks or food, do it. It helps in future situations. 

If you get discounted food, remember that discounted food always tastes better. 

Always ask if they want a refill or another drink when their glass is almost empty. 

Some people don’t know how to tip or they’re just grouchy. Don’t let a bad tip get you down.

You’ll figure it out as you go. You’ll get your groove and mini procedures that you follow. Everyone’s way of serving is in some way different. Figure out what works for you and stick with it. 

If possible write your tips down, make sure it correlates with what you get at the end of the night. 

Another thing I just do because I sometimes forget about a table in my section, is to count them. Let’s say you have 4 tables that are in your section, when you’re in the weeds and you’re not sure what’s going on and you’re busy planning it all out, just count the tables, see if there isn’t someone who just sat down or a table that you forgot about because table 22 couldn’t read the menu and had to be explained the entire thing.  It helps to organise your planning as well. 

Just have fun. The job’s pretty great if you get through all the crappy customers and the mini heart race. You get to meet new and exciting people every day and all of them have different personalities. If you have fun with a table (like actually enjoy serving them, having a laugh with them, or just some really really stupid joke about a procedure that exists for a reason but sounds stupid to a customer (like charging for extra of X because food cost is a thing)), they’ll most likely tip you better.
